state: Sellers dominate the immediate structure while price rides the lower Bollinger band.
paragraphs: Sellers hold the immediate advantage as price rests at 59.0, trading below the middle Bollinger band located at 63.25 and sliding along the lower band boundary at 58.23502. The confirmed swing structure is fully aligned to the downside, with price breaking cleanly below the latest confirmed low of 63.0. Recent downward runs match this persistent pressure, maintaining an average span of 2.5 across the last 12 sequences while bullish counter-moves struggle to reach more than an average of 1.67 units. This downward extension is not entirely smooth, however, as choppy conditions and moderate opposing wicks show that control changes hands frequently enough to prevent the decline from operating as a completely clean trend.

Stepping back across the broader history shows that selling pressure has consistently outweighed buying attempts over the 104-run window, where bearish moves averaged 2.48 against 2.14 for bullish advances. Recent behavior tightens that divergence instead of softening it. Across the last 12 sequences, selling runs remain anchored at an average span of 2.5, while counter-moves shrink back to an average of just 1.67 units. This contraction in opposing strength explains why the downside bias retains its grip. Bullish efforts are losing endurance even as the wider decline persists, leaving sellers in charge of the pace without encountering meaningful pushback from buyers.

Price is advancing downward with force, but the background conditions tell a more complicated story about stability. Continuation scores have climbed sharply to 74.4, showing that selling pressure is finding renewed backing as the wider volatility range expands along the lower boundary. Yet this push happens alongside an elevated chop score of 79.3 and a moderate transition reading of 55.3. These conflicting metrics mean the decline is occurring inside an erratic structural backdrop instead of a smooth, orderly trend. Opposing wicks remain active enough to show that buyers are still challenging drops, even if their counter-attacks keep shrinking. Sellers own the momentum, but the internal disorder prevents the move from settling into a clean, effortless path.

Directly below current price at 59.0, where a developing bullish Butterfly pattern rests, the lower Bollinger band sits at 58.23502 alongside confirmed low pivots at 57.0 and 56.0, forming the immediate support area that must absorb ongoing selling pressure. Overhead, a dense cluster provides the first resistance zone between 60.0 and 64.20481, incorporating the regression level at 60.85761, the Butterfly X point at 61.452, the middle Bollinger band at 63.25, and SAR at 64.20481. Within this overhead belt, confirmed pivots at 60.0, 61.0, 62.0, 63.0, and 64.0 mark the internal friction points buyers must clear to challenge the larger trend-control area anchored by the upper Bollinger band at 68.26498.

The broader volatility range remains wide while continuing to expand along the lower band, meaning price has room to extend the move without fresh expansion necessarily building behind every leg. Compression readings have pulled back to 82.2, showing that the volatility envelope is open, though this condition serves as a caution instead of an automatic guarantee that the selloff will maintain its current pace. At the same time, the developing Butterfly pattern sitting right at the 59.0 level introduces active counter-pressure. This harmonic structure does not reverse the bearish reading on its own, but it offers a credible source of resistance to further drops. The downside bias remains strong as long as selling runs dominate counter-attacks and the lower band holds the decline.

Rapid switching, erratic timing, and frequent reversals keep the broader market unresolved despite the heavy selling pressure. That unresolved state fades only when the background becomes more orderly, either through a stable range or through persistent directional control. The current bearish lean becomes more convincing as selling runs repeat with steadier timing and continued structural progress while instability decreases. That lean weakens if opposing buyers gain persistent control, reclaim broken structure by pushing back through the overhead resistance cluster, or extend counter-runs beyond recent limits. A stable range can replace the choppy background without automatically reversing the downside bias, but sellers must maintain their run persistence to keep the current structure valid.
